timeline.text: The adult human skull is made of twenty-two bones: eight cranial bones that enclose the brain, and fourteen facial bones.
Frontal bone. It forms the forehead, the brow ridges, and the front wall of the cranial cavity.
Parietal bones, left and right. Together they form the roof and most of the side walls of the cranium.
Temporal bones, left and right. Each houses the inner ear, the organs of hearing and balance.
Occipital bone. It forms the back wall of the cranium, and the foramen magnum connects it to the spinal cord.
Sphenoid bone. Shaped like a butterfly, it sits at the centre of the cranial base.
Ethmoid bone. Light and small, it lies between the two orbits and forms part of the nasal cavity.
Nasal bones, left and right. Together they form the upper bridge of the nose.
Lacrimal bones, left and right. The smallest bones of the face, they form part of the inner orbital wall and house the lacrimal sac.
Maxillae, left and right. They form the midface, hold the upper teeth, and contain the maxillary sinuses.
Zygomatic bones, left and right. They form the cheekbones, the most prominent bones of the face.
Palatine bones, left and right. They form the back of the hard palate and part of the lateral nasal wall.
Inferior nasal conchae, left and right. Scroll-shaped bones on the lateral nasal wall that warm and humidify the air we breathe.
Vomer. A single midline bone that forms the lower part of the nasal septum.
Mandible. The largest and strongest facial bone, and the only skull bone that moves.
Separated, all twenty-two bones can be seen, each in its own place.
And back together, a complete skull.
Apart, every bone is clear. Together, they protect the brain and shape the face.
